scope: Matched zero-shot versus rank-8 VACE contact adapter on a temporally held-out >=20-second window
summary: The adapter improves local teacher-contact, topology-edge, and edit-region proxies, but fails edit-region quality, topology, and temporal non-regression gates and is visibly wrong in robot scale/identity and flower appearance; full 27.5-second model-only expansion was stopped.
evidence: The blind window uses source frames 594--642, or 24.75--26.75 seconds, with identical input, RGB-alpha-contact control, reference, prompt, seed 20260812, 20 steps, and denoising strength 0.75.
Contact teacher similarity improves from 0.35763 to 0.42496, topology-edge similarity from 0.43617 to 0.45806, and edit-region similarity from 0.12745 to 0.15837.
Temporal teacher similarity regresses from 0.70381 to 0.67921; adapted edit-region similarity is below 0.25 and topology-edge similarity is below 0.50.
The complete held-out proxy decision is PARTIAL and the review sheet shows wrong robot scale/identity plus invented oversized flowers.
lessons: A same-scene LoRA can improve a contact proxy while worsening temporal behavior and failing semantic identity.
Object-track and localized gates prevent high outside-mask similarity from hiding a failed edit region.
A temporally held-out same-scene window is necessary but insufficient evidence of generalization.
limitations: Training uses twelve clips from one scene and one generated teacher with residual hand smear.
The 2-D contact channel cannot supervise depth, force closure, collision safety, or executable robot contact.
No native addressable KV memory or multi-scene cross-morphology curriculum was available in the pinned Wan/VACE runtime.
next_actions: Do not run a full model-only rollout from this checkpoint.
Collect multi-scene, multi-morphology robot RGB-alpha data with depth/contact supervision and train on self-generated 5--30-second histories before the next promotion attempt.
